name: Resend bounce webhook + pause retention clock on bounce
description:
P1. No Resend webhook route exists, so bounces and spam complaints are 100% invisible. resend@6.12.3 already ships webhooks.verify() (index.d.mts:2108, SYNCHRONOUS, returns typed WebhookEventPayload) and svix@1.92.2 is already a transitive dep, so no new dependency.

SUBSCRIBE TO: email.bounced, email.complained. ONLY. email.delivered/opened/clicked are noise at ~8 orders/week and no gating decision reads them. Note Gmail does not reliably emit complaint webhooks, so silence is not proof of no complaints.

CAUTION: EmailBounce is typed {message: string; subType: string; type: string} (index.d.mts:1869-1873). 'Permanent' vs 'Transient' is a runtime string convention the SDK does NOT narrow. Write an explicit guard with a safe default for unrecognised values - wrong direction either suppresses a good address or keeps mailing a dead one.

AUTOMATIC on hard bounce: stop retries, flag the row for the Needs-You queue, and PAUSE THE 90-DAY RETENTION CLOCK. That last one is a real bug found by the council: readingRetention.ts:16-21 measures from deliveredAt, which deliverOne writes via markSubmissionDelivered BEFORE the send. A customer whose email bounced can have their access window expire before ever seeing a link, and R2 deletes the audio+PDF ~120d post-upload regardless.

NEVER AUTOMATIC: refund, suppression-list purge. Becky contacts and decides refund; Max purges suppression only on a confirmed corrected address.

KNOWN UNSOLVED GAP, name it in the runbook, do not invent a fix: there is NO fallback contact. Verified - the only customer field taken off the Stripe session is customer_details.address.country (webhook/route.ts:40), and there is not one phone reference in src/lib/booking/ or studio/schemas/. If the email is dead we cannot reach them.

Resend AUP: suspension without warning above 4% bounce or 0.08% complaint. Webhook endpoint auto-disables after 8 failed delivery attempts.

Est 3h.

GIFTS (Max side note 2026-10-03): the gift send email goes to an address the buyer typed, which D1 deletes after sending (gift plan MEMORY/WORK/gift-v1-council/ISA.md). Tag gift sends in Resend with the gift id so a bounce maps back to the gift. Open product question for Max: on a gift-send bounce, tell the buyer and give the resend back? clicked/opened stay off: both need Resend tracking, and email.clicked only fires when links go through Resend's redirect, which would put gift links in Resend's logs. 'Gift opened' already comes from our own redeem step.
result: POST /api/webhooks/resend: Svix-verified, bounced/complained/suppressed/failed recorded as failures, tags submission_id and email_type on customer sends, stale events ignored. Max action: create the webhook in Resend and set RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET per env. Gift bounces not covered (gifts not built).

name: Rich text editors for email body + signoff fields
description:
Becky asked for WYSIWYG editing of email body content (bold, italic, links, paragraph breaks). Currently each email singleton stores body content as plain string/text fields in studio/schemas/email*.ts. Decision: convert body + signoff fields (any multi-line/long-form surface) to Sanity Portable Text. Keep subject + button labels + short labels as simple strings.

Scope:
- studio/schemas/email{OrderConfirmation,Day7Delivery,MagicLink,GiftPurchaseConfirmation,GiftClaim,RecipientIntakeReceived,PrivacyExport}.ts — switch body + signOff field defs to array of [{type:'block'}]
- src/data/defaults.ts — convert string defaults to PortableTextBlock[] shape (1 block per paragraph)
- src/lib/emails/{OrderConfirmation,Day7Delivery,MagicLink,...}.tsx — render Portable Text via @portabletext/to-html or react-email-friendly equivalent; keep token slot rendering ({firstName}, {readingName}, etc.) working inside text spans

- New migration: scripts/migrate-email-bodies-to-portable-text-2026-05.ts — converts existing prod string content -> PortableText shape, idempotent (skip already-converted), additive setIfMissing pattern
- Vitest coverage for the new render path (token substitution + bold/italic preservation)

Acceptance:
- Becky can bold/italic/link text inside body + signoff fields in Studio
- Worker renders emails identically (HTML preserves formatting; tokens still substitute)
- Migration script applied to prod dataset; no editorial content lost

Effort: medium (~3-5h). Touches 7 schemas + 7 components + 1 migration.

name: Stale redirect: /my-gifts -> /my-readings, but v1.16.0 deleted both
description:
next.config.ts:39-47 still redirects /my-gifts -> /my-readings permanently (308). The v1.16.0 strip removed BOTH routes: no src/app/**/my-readings or my-gifts exists, and neither appears in the build manifest.

So the only thing this rule does is add a redirect hop before a 404. A permanent redirect is also cached by browsers and intermediaries, so anyone who ever hit /my-gifts keeps getting sent to a dead URL from cache.

Found while checking whether the deleted /book/{slug}/letter and /intake routes needed redirects. Low severity, trivial fix: delete the rule, or point it at / if /my-gifts was ever linked externally.

Note the redirects() function itself should stay - it is the natural home for any future route-collapse redirects.
result:
FIXED and verified live. Removed the /my-gifts -> /my-readings rule (both routes deleted in v1.16.0, so it was a permanent redirect to a 404). curl now returns a direct 404 for /my-gifts instead of a 308 hop.

Reused the same redirects() block for the routes this epic deletes: /book/:slug/letter and /book/:slug/intake now 308 -> /book/:slug. Verified: /book/soul-blueprint/letter -> /book/soul-blueprint, /book/birth-chart/intake -> /book/birth-chart.

Neither was needed for SEO (both carried robots:{index:false,follow:false}, neither was in sitemap.ts, no email links to them) but they were live in production, so a customer with a bookmarked or open /intake tab now lands on the form instead of a 404.

name: sanityMirror readingRefCache: invalidate on TTL or document-rename signal
description: From code-review 2026-05-25. MEDIUM finding src/lib/booking/persistence/sanityMirror.ts:60-80. Module-scope cache survives the worker isolate lifetime; CF Workers isolate lifetime is non-deterministic. name: Evaluate cross-client email testing tool (Litmus / Email-On-Acid / Resend preview)
description:
PLANNING / EVALUATION subtask. Locked 2026-05-24 by Max ("plan for it now" vs "defer until render bug").

WHY NEEDED
React Email + iframed preview shows Chrome rendering, not Gmail / Outlook / Apple Mail. Email clients strip CSS aggressively (no flexbox-gap, limited @media, no CSS custom properties without fallbacks in most). The iframe-pane preview catches edit-time copy/layout but NOT client-specific rendering bugs. Send-to-test (separate subtask) gives accurate Gmail rendering for Becky's inbox but doesn't cover Outlook desktop / Apple Mail dark mode / Yahoo / etc.

DELIVERABLE
Written eval report at www/MEMORY/WORK/<slug>/CROSS_CLIENT_EVAL.md comparing:

1. Litmus (litmus.com) — industry standard. Pricing tiers (free trial → Basic $99/mo → higher tiers). API + visual diff. 90+ client previews.
2. Email-On-Acid (emailonacid.com) — direct competitor to Litmus. Pricing. Coverage.
3. Resend's built-in preview — currently none in the dashboard; check 2026 state. Free if it exists.
4. Mailchimp's Inbox Inspector (if standalone access still exists).
5. HTMLemail.io / Email Comb minifiers — preprocessing tools that strip non-compatible CSS automatically; cheaper than visual tests, prevents some bugs before they ship.

DECISION CRITERIA
- Coverage breadth (how many clients tested per send).
- Cost vs project scale (~10 customers/month at launch).
- Integration shape: manual upload of HTML vs API webhook vs no-integration-needed (visual-diff a deployed-static-render).
- Whether dark-mode rendering is covered (Outlook + Apple Mail diverge here).

OUTPUT
Recommendation: adopt one + monthly budget, OR defer with explicit trigger (e.g., first customer reports render bug in client X). Then file the follow-up tasks if adopted.

NOT IN SCOPE
- Actual integration (separate subtask if eval recommends adoption).
- Free-tool patchwork as a substitute (e.g., manually opening each email in each client) — that's labor-intensive and doesn't scale; the eval is about tool-buy decision.

TRIGGER FOR EVAL: any time after the iframe-pane swap + send-to-test subtasks land. NOT blocking on launch.
result: Shipped via PR #225 commit 860fd58 on release/v1.5.0 as docs/CROSS_CLIENT_EMAIL_EVAL.md. Compared Litmus, Email-On-Acid, Resend native preview, Mailchimp Inbox Inspector, and CSS preprocessing tools. Decision: DEFER ADOPTION. At ~10 customers/month launch volume, $74-99/mo doesn't pencil. PR #226's send-to-test action covers Max's primary inbox. React Email's table-based render already conservative on CSS. Promotion trigger documented: 1+ customer render-bug report in 30-day window, OR 100+ customer emails/month, OR new template with non-trivial CSS, OR brand redesign. When trigger fires, pick Email-On-Acid Starter ~$74/mo over Litmus.

name: Astro: distinguish retryable from terminal failure (generatedAt loop)
description:
Filed under the ASTRO epic, deliberately OUT of the delivery-observability release per Max (2026-08-01).

generateAstroChart returns null ONLY when ASTRO_API_TOKEN/URL are unset (:65) - that case retries correctly. EVERY other failure, including a service 503 (:98) and a request timeout/throw (:117), returns an object carrying generatedAt alongside error (:71-78). backfillAstroCharts.ts:19-22 excludes anything with defined(astroChart.generatedAt), so a TRANSIENT failure becomes permanently sticky and only a manual Studio Regenerate recovers it.

The bug is NOT 'failures are stamped as done'. It is that the code does not distinguish retryable from terminal. A malformed birth date should stick and wait for a human, exactly as the comment at :58 intends. A 30-second service blip should not permanently cost a chart. Same code path, opposite correct behaviours.

DONE: retry on transport errors and 5xx; stick on validation and 4xx.

Same defect class as the delivery epic (4s6dkgsf): terminal marker written on intent, not confirmed outcome. Self-limits to one customer, which is why it is not release-blocking.

Est 1h.

name: EPIC: Delivery observability + failure recovery
description:
Delivery failures are currently invisible and the Studio desk view actively reports success on a failed send. Root cause is ONE defect class with five instances: a terminal marker is written on intent rather than on confirmed outcome.

INSTANCES:
1. deskStructure.ts:96-118 filters Delivered on defined(deliveredAt) alone; Becky sets that field herself at upload, so a failed delivery displays as green.
2. generateAstroChart.ts:71-78,98,117 stamps generatedAt on failure branches, so backfillAstroCharts.ts:19-22 never retries. (Astro is OUT of this release - see astro branch.)
3. webhook/route.ts:26-32,108 returns 200 after the not-found early return, defeating Stripe retry.
4. custom-worker.ts withMonitor reports ok unless the callback throws, so a zero-delivery run checks in green.
5. readingRetention.ts:16-21 measures the customer 90-day access window from deliveredAt, written before the send, so a failed delivery burns the window and R2 deletes assets ~120d post-upload.

EVIDENCE BASE: 4 research agents (Resend deliverability, cron observability, codebase failure-mode map, non-technical alerting UX) + 5-persona 3-round council. When opened, both render the OS-native option list — bright white background, system font, sharp corners — which clashes visually with the cream + Cormorant + rounded-pill design language used everywhere else in the form (see screenshot 2026-05-28). Goal: option lists should match the booking form's design tokens (cream surface, Cormorant labels, j-rose hover, rounded corners, soft shadow).

Approach options:
  (a) Replace native <select> with Radix UI Select (or Headless UI Listbox) — fully stylable, a11y handled, keyboard nav works. Recommended.
  (b) Try CSS-only via appearance:none + custom arrow — does NOT restyle the dropdown panel itself (browsers won't let you), so only fixes the closed-state chrome, not the open option list. Won't satisfy the ask.
  (c) Hybrid — keep native for accessibility but accept the visual mismatch. Status-quo.

For DatePicker specifically: react-day-picker's captionLayout="dropdown" can be replaced by passing custom components via the components prop (MonthsDropdown, YearsDropdown) so the brand Select component renders in the caption slot.

Surfaces:

name: Mechanical comment-narration guard (vitest scanner)
description:
Recurrence-prevention for feedback_comments_over_logged. The rule is in memory + applied at session-load but it keeps getting violated across sessions and by dispatched Engineer agents. Memory alone isn't enough; need a mechanical guard that runs in CI.

Implementation: small vitest scanner in src/scanners/ following the SANDBOX_EMAIL_PREFIXES pattern (PR #214). Fails CI on:

- Multi-line comment blocks over 4 consecutive '//' lines in non-test source files (catches narration headers)

Allowlist: docs/, MEMORY/, *.test.*, *.md. Inline override marker for rare legitimate case (e.g., '// allow-narrate').

Covers: src/, scripts/, migrations/, studio/. Why mechanical: memory-only rules don't reliably gate code generation; this catches both my own drift and dispatched-agent output.

name: Header = card title block (tag/name/price) absolutely centred + per-card anchors
description:
PRD step 5. REV-2 LOCKED 2026-07-29 (Max chose D3 from header-variations.html). Pill switcher CANCELLED; the earlier one-line 'name + price' treatment is also superseded.

WHAT SHIPS:

1. BookingFlowHeader.tsx - centre slot stops being the 'Josephine Soul Readings' wordmark and becomes the HOMEPAGE CARD'S THREE-LINE STACK, verbatim recipe from ReadingCard.tsx:50-58:
   tag  -> tracking-[0.22em] uppercase text-j-accent font-body | phone .6rem/.18em, desktop .68rem/.22em
   name -> font-display font-light italic leading-tight | phone 1.25rem (20px), desktop 2.4rem (38.4px = the card's clamp top)
   price-> font-display italic text-j-accent | phone 1rem, desktop 1.5rem
   Label, not a link. Nothing in the header navigates except Back.

2. *** ABSOLUTE CENTRING, NOT GRID. LOAD-BEARING. ***
   .header { position:relative; display:flex; align-items:center; min-height:116px }
   .back   { position:relative; z-index:2 }
   .title  { position:absolute; left:50%; top:50%; transform:translate(-50%,-50%) }
   Why: 'flex justify-between' (today's code) measured 35px off centre, and grid-cols-[1fr_auto_1fr] measured 7px off on the long name forms - both let Back's width push the block. Absolute centring is immune. VERIFIED 0px horizontal / -0.5px vertical on every reading and both name forms at 375 and 900.

3. PHONE SIZE IS DICTATED BY BACK, DESKTOP IS NOT. At 375 the worst case (Akashic Record Reading ) is 171px wide and clears Back by 28px; at card scale the same block is 246px and lands INSIDE Back. At 900 the full-scale block is 329px, clears by 204px. So: compact on phone, card-literal on desktop. Header 116px phone / 150px desktop.

4. Back mark = drawn 9x14 SVG chevron, NOT the '<' U+2039 angle quote the code ships today (at 14px it reads as stray punctuation). Keep >=44px touch target. NOTE the current source literal is U+2039, not U+2018.

5. ReadingIcon glyph above the tag is AVAILABLE BUT OFF by default. Verified by zoom: it renders correctly at header size with its shipped 1.2 stroke - no size-aware variant needed, do NOT bump the stroke. Adds ~32px to the block if enabled.

6. HomePageView.tsx:120 - id="reading-{slug}" on the <li> + scroll-margin-top MEASURED against the fixed nav (Navigation.tsx:103). backHref becomes /#reading-{slug}.

7. intake/page.tsx:22-44 - DROP the eyebrow. VARIANT_COPY collapses to a per-slug subtitle map, shared title.

8. D8 - 'Continue to payment' centred below the page indicator on mobile.

*** FOLLOW-ON THIS DECISION FORCES: *** at 20px the phone title is SMALLER than the card's 'A few things, before we begin.' heading (29.6px) directly below it, so the page title is smaller than its subtitle. Bring that heading down or cut it. Max is aware; not yet decided.

NO CODE CHANGES for the swap: useDraftRestore.ts:99-106 keys on getLastReadingId() vs the route param, so homepage -> different 'Book now' preserves SWAP_PRESERVED_KEYS and fires SwapToast unchanged.

CLAUDE.md: 'Reading-change navigation - entry page only' needs a WORDING change (affordance = homepage card CTA), not a mechanism change.

Price contrast inherited not introduced: gold on cream = 2.23:1, fails the 3:1 large-text threshold at desktop size, exactly as the homepage card already does (gk2etjdy).

SPECIMEN: MEMORY/WORK/20260729-booking-funnel-collapse/header-variations.html - self-contained, real fonts inlined, open directly. D3 is locked; D1/D2 kept for the record.

DONE + browser-verified at a real 375px viewport (iframe-framed page, so media queries responded to a genuine 375px width).

HomePageView <li> got id=reading-{slug} + scroll-mt-[96px] (72px fixed nav + 24px gap). Eyebrow dropped, VARIANT_COPY collapsed to a shared title + per-slug subtitle. MEASURED (real 375px, all three readings): horizontal offset 0px, vertical -0.5px, header 116px, name 20px, tag 9.6px, price 16px, no overlap with Back, no horizontal scroll. Desktop at 1512px: 0px / -0.5px, header 150px, name 38.4px. The PRD's centring claim reproduced EXACTLY.

PRD FIGURE THAT WAS OPTIMISTIC: predicted worst case 171px clearing Back by 28px. name: Max decisions before the header work lands
description:
PRD section 4. Reconciled 2026-07-29 after Max locked D3 (REV-2).

SETTLED BY THE D3 CHOICE - do not re-ask:
- Price in the header: YES. D3's block is tag/name/price, so choosing it answered this.
- Panel-open across navigation, desktop bar width: cancelled with the switcher (REV-1).

STILL OPEN, decide before 5xkgbm7x lands:

1. RESUME POSITION. currentPage IS persisted in the draft envelope, but useDraftRestore.ts:124 deliberately discards it and forces page 0. Restoring it is a one-line revert of an intentional decision. Low value if Soul Blueprint ends up the only multi-page reading.

2. DRAFT TTL. Drafts expire 72h after last edit (DRAFT_TTL_MS). Raise it if 'continue where you left off' should survive longer.

3. RESUME AFFORDANCE. Nothing tells a returning visitor their answers were kept; only DiscardDraftButton appears. The specimen's 'Resuming a draft' state is a proposal, not approved.

4. NAME FORM: short ('Soul Blueprint', matches the homepage card) vs '... Reading' ('Soul Blueprint Reading', matches the Stripe line item and metadata). D3 handles both - worst case at 375 is 171px, clearing Back by 28px. Whichever you pick should be what the header shows.

5. BACK DESTINATION: /#reading-{slug} (per-card anchor, the default written into PRD D5) vs /#readings (section heading). Alfred picked the per-card anchor; router.back() was rejected because it breaks on a cold deep link, the dominant entry pattern from TikTok.

6. NON-STICKY HEADER: PRD D6 keeps it relative/scrolling-away, as today. Only loss is a sticky Back; PageNav's own back button covers mid-form.

7. GLYPH above the tag: on or off. Verified it renders fine at the shipped 1.2 stroke, so this is taste. Adds ~32px to the block.

8. BECKY: sign off on the folded letter copy - it is her voice.

MOVED TO THE STYLING PASS (681ra7bq), not blocking 5xkgbm7x: the header-title-smaller-than-heading inversion, and the overall preamble length.

name: Automate 3-year reading-content deletion
description:
Privacy policy declares reading content deleted after 3 years (READING_CONTENT_RETENTION_YEARS=3) but nothing enforces it. cleanup cron only handles unpaid intake (30d) + R2 photo (90d); paid Sanity submissions (intake answers, voice note, PDF assets) persist until manual Studio cascade. Compliance risk: policy states a deletion period it does not enforce.

Plan (reuse, do not rebuild):
1. Add a 4th pass to the cleanup cron (or sibling): select paid submissions older than READING_CONTENT_RETENTION_YEARS from paidAt/createdAt.
2. Reuse content-deletion half of cascadeDeleteUser / deleteCustomerData: delete Sanity submission (voiceNote+readingPdf assets + responses[]) + residual R2 photo; EXPLICITLY skip financial_records (6yr HMRC, migration 0005 documents the asymmetry).
3. Do NOT fire Stripe/Brevo/Mixpanel redaction — this is retention-expiry, not Art.17 erasure. Confirm scoping with privacy counsel.
4. Summary log + idempotency guard.
5. Test: >3yr paid submission content deleted while financial_records row survives; staging e2e against back-dated fixture.

Context + corrected policy: www/docs/PRIVACY_POLICY_RECONCILIATION.md

Max 2026-10-03: build this after the gift flow (85v0vzq0) is in production. Include gift_codes rows (buyer name, note, emails) in the retention pass; plan in MEMORY/WORK/gift-v1-council/ISA.md.

name: my-readings: Readings tab unreachable for gift-only accounts (defaultTab=gifts no-op)
description: Smoke 2026-05-27 staging, maxgertzen@gmail.com (0 readings, 3 gifts). Clicking the Readings tab does nothing. Root cause src/app/my-readings/_shared/LibraryView.tsx:104 'const activeTab = pathname === GIFTS_PATH ? gifts : defaultTab'. When readings empty + gifts present, pickDefaultTab returns 'gifts', so at READINGS_PATH (/my-readings) activeTab=defaultTab='gifts'. handleChange (line 106-112) only router.push-es when nextPath !== pathname; selecting 'readings' targets /my-readings which already === pathname, so push is skipped (no-op). And activeTab has no client state to hold the explicit selection, so it always recomputes to defaultTab. Net: gift-only purchasers can never open the (empty) Readings tab. Masked when user has >=1 reading (defaultTab=readings, paths differ). Fix options: (a) when defaultTab=gifts redirect /my-readings -> /my-readings/gifts so path is the single source of truth and Readings click navigates cleanly; (b) hold activeTab in client useState initialized from defaultTab so handleChange updates state even when path is unchanged. Needs a test for the gift-only case. Phase 2 surface.
result: Closed at the root by PR #208 (dex 0bjxc38w): removing the tab strip eliminates the unreachable-tab path entirely. Both sections now render unconditionally for gift-only accounts.

name: T3 astro client lib: fetch + extraction + fail-closed + R2
description: src/lib/booking/astro/ (new): typed client for POST /v1/astro/full?include=context,image,html. Extract birthDate(date)/birthTime(time)/place(placeAutocomplete) from responses[] by fieldType, not key. Missing time → 12:00:00 + birthTimeKnown:false. FAIL CLOSED: if ASTRO_API_TOKEN missing/empty, do not send (VPS fail2ban 5x401→1h ban); never retry on 401. Client timeout <30s. Authorization: Bearer <token> verbatim. Upload base64 PNG to R2 (src/lib/r2.ts, images.withjosephine.com), return URL. Capture failure as error string. Env via getCloudflareContext({async:true}). Unit tests: extraction, noon fallback, fail-closed. ISC-5,6,7,10,11,14, anti ISC-A-3.
result: astro/extractBirthInputs.ts (select-by-fieldType, empty-time→noon+birthTimeKnown:false, date/time normalize) + astro/generateAstroChart.ts (fail-closed null when token/URL absent — never sends a known-401; 25s timeout <30s nginx; posts context,image,structured; uploads PNG to R2 via putObject + R2_PUBLIC_ORIGIN; captures failures as error, never throws). 12 unit tests green (extraction cases + fail-closed + happy-path + non-2xx + missing-data). Added ASTRO_API_TOKEN/ASTRO_API_URL to EnvVar. typecheck clean.

name: Gift flow v1: own gift code + link (option D)
description:
Design locked 2026-10-03 (Max). Mockup (source of truth for screens and copy): https://claude.ai/artifact/FENmNtqiW7yrEgZaHHzHZU (version 7, "Design locked"). Old flow on release/v2.0.0 is reference for copy and email layouts only.

Gift = our own code in D1, plus a link. The recipient never sees Stripe and nobody logs in.

Architecture (Max: states resolved on load, no live updates):
- The code is created with the pending gift row when the gift sheet is sent, and switched on when Stripe confirms payment, by whichever comes first: the gift thank-you page (server render, it already reads the Stripe session in fetchThankYouSessionSnapshot) or the webhook. Both idempotent. The thank-you page renders the code on first load. Slow payment methods (bank debit) show "the code comes by email as soon as it clears".
- The gift link is /gift/<code>: a server-rendered route that checks the code before the page is sent, then renders the booking form in gift mode (valid) or a short message page with no form (used, no longer active, not found). noindex. The static /book/<slug> page is untouched (stays SSG and indexable). Code in the path: add it to Sentry URL redaction (src/lib/sentry-client.ts); Mixpanel already drops URLs; check Clarity and Resend click tracking.
- Redeem gift sheet and the last-page code field validate on submit, then go to /gift/<code>; the draft is kept (same reading id).
- No client-side checking states anywhere.

Buyer:
- /book/[slug]: a "Giving or redeeming a gift" fold row with the gift icon, inside the form card right before the intro ("Before I read for you..."), same style as the reading block's fold row, smaller. Open: "Buying it for someone? Send it as a gift" and "Have a code? Redeem gift". Homepage cards unchanged.
- Gift sheet over the page (no new route): 3 steps, buyer first name (required, max 80), optional note (280 characters, counter from 220, rose from 260, strip {...} tags), buyer checkbox (label pending legal calls below), "Continue to payment". Redirects to the reading's existing Payment Link with client_reference_id=gift_<id>. No new Payment Links.
- Stripe webhook and reconcile cron: client_reference_id starting with gift_ switches the gift on and sends the buyer confirmation email. Today both look the id up as a submission and log a warning.
- Gift thank-you page, one column: code, Copy link, Share (Web Share API; hidden where the browser has none, for example Firefox desktop), the note with "Edit note" (until the gift is opened), "Send it by email from Josephine" opening the form in place.
- Send form: recipient name and email. From Josephine <hello@withjosephine.com>; replies go to hello@ like every other email (Max: no reply-to buyer). Sent now only. One send plus one resend; the resend reopens with the name only, the address is deleted after sending. Errors: invalid email, buyer's own email. Turnstile. Clarity masking on the note and send form fields.
- Buyer confirmation email: code, link, "Share on WhatsApp", "Send it by email from Josephine" button to /gift/send#<send secret> (separate from the gift code; states: ready, already sent, gift opened, not valid).
- No email after Josephine sends the gift. Email "Anna opened your gift" when the recipient submits.

Recipient:
- Josephine's email ("A reading, waiting for you"), note card only when there is a note, "Open your gift", the code as a fallback line.
- /gift/<code>, valid: note card at the top of the form card, price line "A gift, already paid", gift row and "Not sure this is the one?" box hidden, page line "· a gift from Dana". Code kept with the draft.
- Redeem gift sheet: empty, wrong code, code for another reading (link to it). 5 wrong tries then a wait. Code field on the last page above "Continue to payment" as a second place.
- Last page with a gift: "Gift code ... applied · Remove", "Nothing to pay. This reading is a gift from Dana.", button "Send my details". At submit the server checks the code again, marks it used and the submission paid in one step (new paid-by-gift path in applyPaidEvent; reconcile must skip it). Race: "This gift was opened a moment ago..." with answers kept.
- Gift thank-you page and gift confirmation email. Day-7 delivery unchanged, to the intake email.

Becky in Studio:
- Gift submissions: "Gift from <buyer>" in the desk list, read-only gift fields. The note is deleted when the gift is opened.
- Read-only Gifts list copied from D1 by a cron.
- Gift Settings document: every visitor-facing string, the share message. Gift emails are their own documents. Defaults in src/data/defaults.ts.
- Presentation: a "Gift pages" group in studio/components/PreviewNavigator.tsx, one entry per state (gift row and sheets, opened with note, no note, already opened, no longer active, not found, buyer thank-you, recipient thank-you), routes under /preview/gift/..., built from a sample gift (never a real code), every gift string with edit overlays.
- Same release: oo4wxk3e "Send reading now".

Legal decisions (Max, 2026-10-03): gifts are non-refundable and gift codes do not expire, as in the existing terms. Readings are digital content for entertainment. Consent checkboxes unchanged: the buyer ticks the existing cooling-off checkbox (COOLING_OFF_CONSENT_LABEL) in the gift sheet; the recipient sees the existing 3 checkboxes. Legal pages: add the gift lines in the existing wording (gifts welcome, one reading, does not expire, non-refundable). Privacy additions: a short notice line in the recipient email (details given by the buyer, used for this email only, deleted after sending), Resend in the US processors list, and the recipient told about the "gift opened" email before she submits.

Not yet checked: the site Button's letter-spacing makes uppercase labels sit off-centre (seen on Share in the mockup).

name: Add top nav / back-to-site affordance on /my-readings (auth-gated surface)
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-28 via staging walk. /my-readings (and likely /listen, /gift/intake, /thank-you) renders with NO top nav, NO logo, NO back-to-home link. Root src/app/layout.tsx contains zero header/Navigation, only body styling + analytics + draft tools. /my-readings has no layout.tsx of its own. MyReadingsView.tsx only renders a section <header> (the 'Gifts' / 'Mine' heading). UX gap: a user landing on /my-readings via a magic-link email has no obvious way back to the rest of the site.

DECISION NEEDED (before build):
  (a) Light top-bar with logo + 'home' link, auth-gated surfaces only (/my-readings, /listen, etc.) — minimal, doesn't compete with the brand quietness
  (b) Full marketing nav (same as home page) on auth-gated surfaces — may feel over-decorated
  (c) Footer-only back-link, no top nav — minimal

Also audit which surfaces share this gap: /my-readings, /my-readings/welcome, /my-readings/gifts (308 redirect), /listen/[id], /gift/intake, /gift/claim/[token], /thank-you/[readingId].

Not launch-blocking but it's a noticeable UX rough edge — escalate to launch-blocking only if Max says so.

name: 90-day reading access policy + R2 lifecycle (retention parity)
description:
Today: listen-page HMAC tokens default to 1-year expiry (LISTEN_TOKEN_SECRET config); CheckEmailCard re-issues indefinitely; R2 voice-note + PDF objects have NO lifecycle rule. Net: customer access = forever, data retention = forever. GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) data minimization exposure.

New policy (locked 2026-05-24 with Max): **90-day access window per reading**, then no self-service. After 90d: customer must email Josephine for manual re-issue (admin route already exists at /api/internal/issue-magic-link).

Scope:
- src/lib/auth/listenSession.ts (or wherever LISTEN_TOKEN expiry is set at mint time) — change default from 1y -> 90d
- src/lib/auth/users.ts magic-link mint path -> 90d expiresAt
- src/components/CheckEmailCard/ -> hide or 404 when submission deliveredAt + 90d < now; show 'expired — email hello@withjosephine.com' affordance
- src/app/my-readings/page.tsx — each reading row past 90d: replace 'Open' CTA with 'Expired — email hello@withjosephine.com' (link to mailto with subject prefilled including readingId)
- src/lib/emails/Day7Delivery.tsx + EMAIL_DAY7_DELIVERY_DEFAULTS — copy update to mention 90d window: 'Your link is good for the next 90 days. After that, just email me and I'll send a fresh one.'
- R2 lifecycle: configure rule on the voice-note + PDF prefix(es) in the prod bucket (withjosephine-booking-photos? or a separate readings bucket — verify). Expire objects 120d after upload (90d access + 30d grace for slow-listening customers + admin re-issue window before deletion).
- Confirm /api/internal/issue-magic-link still works as the admin escape hatch (already exists per grep)
- Privacy policy + Terms text update — define the 90d retention window explicitly
- Vitest: token mint with 90d expiry; CheckEmailCard expired branch; /my-readings expired-row branch
- E2e spec: customer with delivered_at older than 90d can't re-issue self-service; admin can

R2 audit needed before implementation:
- Where do voice-note + PDF actually live? withjosephine-booking-photos? josephine-backups? Or Sanity Assets? (booking-photos shows 0 objects in your screenshot; staging has 3 in withjosephine-booking-photos-staging)
- Confirm key prefix structure so lifecycle rule scopes correctly (don't accidentally expire intake photos)

Acceptance:
- New reading delivered today -> listen-page HMAC URL works for 90d, then 404s
- Day-7 email copy mentions 90d window
- CheckEmailCard self-service disappears past 90d, replaced with email-Josephine CTA
- /my-readings rows past 90d show expired state with mailto
- Admin route can mint fresh link for stale readings
- R2 lifecycle rule deletes voice-note + PDF objects ~120d after upload
- Privacy policy text updated to declare 90d retention

Effort: high (~6-9h). Touches auth mint, UI affordances, email copy, R2 infra, legal docs. Worth its own sub-PR.

name: Clarity-Bot vs CF Bot Fight Mode — only if playbacks render unstyled
description: CONDITIONAL / watch-item. Microsoft Clarity uses a server-side 'Clarity-Bot' (User-Agent: Clarity-Bot) to fetch site CSS so replays render styled. On our CF plan (Free zone) there is NO per-bot allowlist toggle — that lives in Super Bot Fight Mode (Pro+). A WAF skip rule does NOT help: on Free, Bot Fight Mode runs BEFORE WAF and can't be WAF-skipped (see memory cf-bot-fight-mode). LIKELY A NON-ISSUE: Clarity captures DOM + same-origin CSS from the actual visitor's browser during recording; Clarity-Bot's fetch is mainly for cross-origin/uncacheable assets, and our CSS is same-origin. ACTION: do NOT weaken Bot Fight Mode preemptively. After the consent/recording fix ships and sessions flow, open a few recordings — if they render UNSTYLED (raw HTML), THEN: (1) check CF dashboard Security > Events for challenged Clarity-Bot requests, (2) verify whether Clarity-Bot is a CF verified bot (verified bots are permitted by BFM), (3) only then weigh turning BFM off for the asset paths or a plan upgrade. If playbacks render fine, close this.

name: Security: public requests with a cf-cron header pass cron auth
description: isCronRequestAuthorized returns true for any request carrying a cf-cron header (src/lib/booking/cron-auth.ts:10). The header is set by our own scheduled handler (custom-worker.ts:65), not by Cloudflare; the comment at custom-worker.ts:37-40 assumes CF only sets it on scheduled invocations. Nothing strips it from public requests in the composed fetch handler. If Cloudflare passes the header through, anyone can run /api/cron/* (cleanup, reconcile, day-7, day-7-deliver incl. ?force=<id>, which sends with no already-sent check, backup). Not probed: any probe runs a cron route on production. Proposed fix: the composed fetch handler deletes cf-cron from incoming requests before handler.fetch (scheduled dispatch calls handler.fetch directly so it keeps working), plus a unit test. Found by the gift build-docs council 2026-10-03.
result: Shipped as PR #339 (v1.20.2), squash 770bf50, production deploy and smoke green 2026-10-03. Worker fetch entry strips cf-cron from public requests (withoutCronHeader in cron-auth.ts); scheduled dispatch builds its request with scheduledCronRequest and keeps the header. Worker wiring test in cron-auth.worker.test.ts. Follow-ups in tl6kchsk (preview URLs, bearer-only scheduled dispatch, stale middleware comment).

Two engineering scopes:
- The user-context join + fallback handling for stranger-with-no-submission cases
- MagicLink component refactor to vars+applyTokens pattern
Both filed for a separate session.

name: Send-to-test doc action (env-var recipient allowlist)
description:
ADDITIVE to the iframe-pane swap — gives Becky a real-world cross-client render check by sending the rendered email to a pre-approved inbox.

DECISION (locked 2026-05-24 by Max): recipient allowlist lives as an env var on the Worker (ALLOWED_PREVIEW_RECIPIENTS comma-separated), NOT in Sanity siteSettings. Rationale: Studio compromise can't widen the allowlist; rotating recipients = deploy. Faster + safer security boundary.

WHAT
1. Studio doc-action: studio/actions/sendEmailPreview.ts. Available on each of the 8 email singletons. Title: "Send preview to inbox…". Disabled if doc has unpublished changes (force publish first to preview the published copy; current draft preview already lives in the iframe).
2. Action UI: <Dialog> with a select dropdown of allowlisted recipients (fetched from a new worker endpoint that returns the env-var list — never expose the raw env var to Studio bundle).
3. New worker endpoint: POST /api/admin/send-email-preview. Body: { type, recipient }. Auth: ADMIN_API_KEY header (same pattern as existing studio/actions/resendCustomerEmail.ts). Validates recipient is in ALLOWED_PREVIEW_RECIPIENTS env-var before send. Re-uses src/lib/resend.tsx send functions with the current published Sanity content for that type (NOT defaults — Becky is previewing her edited copy).
4. New worker endpoint: GET /api/admin/list-preview-recipients (auth: ADMIN_API_KEY). Returns the allowlist for the dropdown.
5. Audit row written to deletion_log-equivalent (or a new admin_actions log) per send: { actor: "studio-admin", action: "preview_send", emailType, recipient, sentAt }. Same shape as cascadeDeleteUser audit.
6. Rate-limit: re-use the existing WAF rate-limit on /api/admin/* (rl-josephine-api-write-paths covers it implicitly once the path matches) OR add an in-worker per-recipient cooldown (3 sends per recipient per email-type per 24h, mirroring the existing resend-customer-email cooldown).

PRECEDENT
- studio/actions/resendCustomerEmail.ts (existing — published 2026-05-18 in v1.1.0) is the closest pattern. Lift its shape (auth header, audit write, cooldown).
- See www/MEMORY/WORK/20260517-220000_phase-7-email-sanity-cms/PRD.md for the D-4 origin/referer auth posture (this endpoint can use the stronger ADMIN_API_KEY since it's not iframe-loaded).

DOES NOT BLOCK iframe-pane swap or seed migration — strictly additive. Can ship in PR-A1 if scope allows, OR as a follow-up PR-A3.
result: Shipped via PR #226 commit 0ed9e77 on release/v1.5.0. Studio 'Send preview to inbox...' doc action on 12 customer email singletons. New admin routes: GET /api/admin/list-preview-recipients + POST /api/admin/send-email-preview (x-admin-token auth, REFUSED(404) on auth fail). ALLOWED_PREVIEW_RECIPIENTS env var documented in wrangler.jsonc; unset = 503 + dialog shows 'not configured' (fail-closed). New audit event admin_email_preview_sent. New EmailSubType admin_email_preview. Subject prefixed with [PREVIEW] so test renders to shared inbox cannot be mistaken for real customer emails. Per the simplify polish commit 27c65aa, sendEmailPreview routes through canonical sendOrSkip (sandbox-prefix guard, RESEND_DRY_RUN, x-e2e-resend-dry-run header, cached client, redacted logging, serverTrack). Per-recipient cooldown deferred — WAF rate-limit (5 req/10s/IP) + admin-token + env-allowlist combination is sufficient defense-in-depth at v1.5.0 volume. MAX-ACTION POST-MERGE: set ALLOWED_PREVIEW_RECIPIENTS worker secret on staging + prod (value: hello@withjosephine.com,maxgertzen+withjosephine-preview@gmail.com) per SESSION_BOOT.

name: Sanity validation harness — catch schema-vs-data drift locally + CI
description:
Max-flagged 2026-05-24 after Day-7 email schema validation errors surfaced in production Studio. Migration script existed (scripts/migrate-email-bodies-to-portable-text-2026-05.mts) but wasn't required to run pre-deploy, so production data drifted from schema. Required two manual migration runs this session (staging + production) AFTER Max saw the validation banner in Studio.

==== BUILD SCOPE ====

(1) Script: pnpm sanity:validate <staging|production>
- Connects to Sanity via SANITY_READ_TOKEN
- Walks each known singleton (10 customer-facing emails + pages per scripts/seed-customer-emails-and-pages.mts)
- For each field in each schema, asserts actual value type matches schema expected type
- Specifically catches: type 'text' (string) where schema expects array of block (PortableText)
- Exit code non-zero on drift + per-field summary report

(2) Wire (1) into CI as POST-DEPLOY check that fails the release-branch CI if deployed worker code expects shapes the dataset doesn't supply. Add as a job in .github/workflows/ci.yml after the deploy-staging job.

(3) For schema-touching PRs: REQUIRE the migration script be runnable + dry-run-mode verified. Add to PR template or to sentry-skills:pr-writer description guidance.

(4) Inverse check: schema deprecations should not leave orphan data on existing docs. Specifically catch the zombie 'consent' field type in studio/schemas/formField.ts noted in CLAUDE.md known pitfalls section.

==== CONTEXT FROM TONIGHT ====

The validation drift compounded the email-preview blank debugging. Schema expected Array, doc held String, Sanity Studio displayed validation banners for every doc, Max thought it was a render bug, then we found the migration step had been skipped on prod. Both problems would have been caught by an automated pre-publish/post-deploy validation pass.
result: Shipped via commit 345e6fa on release/v1.2.1. scripts/sanity-validate.mts + sibling contract module + CI post-deploy job (sanity-validate-staging, needs deploy-staging). Three severity categories: DRIFT (fails CI), MISSING (warning), WARNING (zombie consent probe). Final staging run: drift=0 missing=2 warnings=0.

name: Gift flow v1: dev council on implementation, security and failure handling
description:
Next session (Max, 2026-10-03): hand the locked gift design to a dev council that decides how to build it. Inputs: dex 85v0vzq0 (full spec), mockup https://claude.ai/artifact/FENmNtqiW7yrEgZaHHzHZU (version 7, "Design locked"), binding constraints in CLAUDE.md, the existing codebase. The design is locked; the council may improve the implementation, not reopen product or legal decisions (no expiry, no refunds, consents unchanged).

Members: a lead dev who knows this stack (Next.js on CF Workers via OpenNext, D1, Durable Objects, Sanity + Presentation, Stripe Payment Links, Resend, crons); a security reviewer; a Sanity/Studio specialist (Gift Settings, Presentation previews for every gift state, Gifts list, oo4wxk3e "Send reading now"); a QA lead (feeds the test plan); a skeptic for scope and PR size.

Evidence rule (CLAUDE.md): every point cites a code path, test, vendor doc or prior incident.

Must decide and document:
- Data model: D1 gift_codes migration (code stored hashed, status, reading, buyer name/email, note, send secret, stripe session id, timestamps), and what mirrors to Sanity.
- Routes and endpoints: gift sheet POST, /gift/[code] server route (noindex, renders the booking form in gift mode or a message page), /gift/send, redeem check, submit with a gift.
- Payment: code made with the pending row, switched on by the thank-you page or the webhook, whichever first; reconcile cron branch; paid-by-gift path in applyPaidEvent.
- Security: code generation and entropy, brute force and rate limits, Turnstile, enumeration (same response for not found vs used where it matters), the code in the /gift path (logs, Sentry redaction, referrer), send secret as a capability link, email abuse (one send + one resend), note sanitising ({...} tags, escaping), PII retention (recipient email deleted after send, note deleted at opening), Clarity masking.
- What can go wrong and how each is handled: webhook late or duplicated, thank-you page and webhook racing, two people redeeming at once, redeem then payment dispute, reading removed or renamed in Sanity, Resend failure, D1 or Sanity down, draft restore with a code, a code typed on the wrong reading.
- Reuse from release/v2.0.0 (copy, email templates, hashing) and what not to bring back.
- PR plan on a release branch: order, size, which ship together with oo4wxk3e.

Output: an implementation plan doc (ISA under www/MEMORY/WORK/), a failure-mode table with handling, a security checklist, and dex subtasks per PR. Then 2 runs of QA (see the QA task).
result: Council of 5, 3 rounds, 2026-10-03. Plan: MEMORY/WORK/gift-v1-council/ISA.md (decisions, migration 0019, activateGift, paid-by-gift submit, 15-item security checklist, failure-mode table with test level and PR, PR plan); transcript CONTEXT/ROUND1-3.md in the same folder. name: Clarity keeps recording after a soft navigation into /gift/ or /thank-you/
description: Found by /code-review on Step 2 (2026-10-04). The Step 2 gate stops ClarityScript from mounting and skips the manual page call on /gift/ and /thank-you/, but Clarity.init never stops on unmount, so a visitor who loaded Clarity on another page and then client-navigates (Link, router.push) into a private link keeps being recorded (code, buyer name, note). No such in-app link exists in Step 2. Before Step 3b or 4 adds one: either make every entry into those paths a full page load, or verify the Clarity tag API for stopping (clarity('stop') is a CDN tag command, not in the @microsoft/clarity npm wrapper) and call it when the pathname becomes private.
result: Confirmed 2026-10-05: no Link, router.push or router.replace points into /gift or /thank-you (rg over src). Entries use window.location.assign (RedeemSheet.tsx:38,69; useIntakeFormHandlers.ts:262,416) or location.href (useIntakeFormHandlers.ts:383), all full page loads, so Clarity never carries over a soft navigation.

name: Preview iframe — image rendering limitation (CORP same-origin)
description:
Tracked from PR #198 (kf1nixad PR-2): the next/image stub currently replaces all relative-path img srcs with a transparent SVG data URL because withjosephine.com sends Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin on /images/* responses, which blocks the sandbox-iframe (null origin) preview from loading the actual images.

Three viable directions when this becomes painful enough:
1. Inline a small set of brand-critical images as base64/SVG data URLs in studio/preview-stubs/ — preview shows real logo, no production change.
2. Mirror /public/images into the Studio bundle under studio/.generated/images/ via a prebuild script, serve them at the iframe-host origin (Studio's own origin) so same-origin holds. More machinery.
3. Relax CORP on /images/* responses in middleware or static-asset handler (risk: weakens prod isolation; needs a real-world threat model first).

Trigger: Becky asks to see the rendered image preview, OR a future preview surface depends on inline imagery for editorial clarity (e.g. brand-decorative SVGs).

Current state: Footer logo + any /public/images/* asset renders as transparent placeholder; layout preserved exactly via width/height/className.

Reference: studio/preview-stubs/next-image.tsx (TRANSPARENT_PIXEL constant + resolveSrc logic).
result: Auto-closed by PR #261 merge (2c36e17f)

name: Add success-marker invariant to CLAUDE.md binding constraints
description:
The single highest-leverage output of the council. One grep-shaped code-review rule that prevents all five instances of this epic's root cause plus the cron's fail-open 200.

PROPOSED TEXT (Nadia, paste-ready):
'A success-marker field (*At, *Id, or any field naming a completed operation) may be written only by the code path that has confirmed the success it names - never before, never on a failure branch, never as a side effect of a different write. Any operation that can fail must leave failure legible (a distinct marker, or none at all) so a retry or backfill job has something to poll. If a line above the assignment can throw, return early, or hit a not-found branch and the assignment still executes, reject it.'

Needs Max's explicit approval before it goes into CLAUDE.md binding constraints.

description: FOLLOW-UP from the picker stacking arc (PR #210 z-30-wrapper-lift then PR #211 portal-rewrite). name: MagicLink — add visible-URL fallback line below the button
description: Code-review MEDIUM finding from 2026-05-25 PR #193: refactor removed the visible-URL fallback from MagicLink.tsx. Old template rendered <Link>{magicLinkUrl}</Link> as clickable + visible body text. New template only exposes the URL via the styled button's href. If a recipient's email client strips the button styling (Outlook Word renderer with no border-radius, dark-mode masking the ink background), they may see only the unstyled label with no way to copy the URL. Auth-recovery is high-stakes; locked-out users = real support load. Fix: add a small 12-13px muted text line below the button: 'Or copy this link: <Link>{magicLinkUrl}</Link>'. Tests should assert the URL appears as both href AND body text. Affects all 3 magic-link variants (one component).
result:

Added a 13px muted "Or copy this link: <URL>" line directly below the magic-link button in MagicLink.tsx. The URL now renders as both the button href AND visible body text, so recipients on hostile clients (Outlook Word renderer, dark-mode masking the ink background, anti-spam button rewriters) can still copy and paste their sign-in link.

All three magic-link variants share this single component (emailMagicLink, emailMagicLinkMyReadings, emailMagicLinkMyGifts), so one change covers every magic-link send. New test asserts URL appears in both linkHrefs and visibleText. Closes the code-review MEDIUM finding from PR #193 review.

name: Intake: should carried-over name/email alone ever make a draft?
description: From the 2026-10-03 /simplify altitude review of card 5C. 5C stops the unmount/pagehide save when the form holds only the values it was restored with (restoredValuesSnapshot from useDraftRestore). The 500ms debounced save still writes carried-over-only values, and valuesUntouched / Save for later compare against defaults, not the restored values. A visit longer than 500ms to reading B therefore still creates a B draft, and the next visit classifies as draft. Wider fix: one baseline (restored snapshot) for every save path; then move setLastReadingId (useDraftRestore.ts:88) into the save path so A -> B -> C still carries name and email. Also from 4B: a reading_switch onto a reading that has a draft is not folded, since entry and has-a-draft share one value; split them if that matters.

name: emailConfirmedAt written only by the existing 6h mirror
description:
P1. Council resolved this unanimously after Tomas withdrew his own counter-proposal.

THREE FIELDS, ONE WRITER EACH:
- deliveredAt (Sanity, Becky's upload, unchanged) = 'assets ready'
- emailsFired[] (D1, cron at send time, sole writer) = 'attempted', source of truth
- emailConfirmedAt (Sanity, NEW, written ONLY by the existing 6-hourly reconcile-mirror) = 'confirmed as of last sync'

REJECTED: a fire-time Sanity write from the cron. Tomas proposed it as 'best-effort'; Nadia showed best-effort means errors are swallowed by design, so a failed write leaves D1 saying sent and Sanity silently unchanged until the mirror overwrites it - turning today's false-positive into a silent false-negative. Ilya adjudicated. D1 stays source of truth per CLAUDE.md binding constraint, no new write path.

Liveness for 'attempted' comes from Studio READING D1 at render time, never writing. 'Sync overdue' is computed (now - firedAt > 6h), not stored.

Est 0.5h.

name: Josephine — edit + preview emails in Studio (Phase 7, paused on branch)
description:
WHAT IT DOES (the feature Josephine sees in Sanity Studio):

Josephine opens any of the 7 customer-facing email singletons in Studio and edits subject / preview / greeting / body / CTA / signoff as plain Sanity fields. The document pane carries a second tab `Preview` (S.view.component(EmailPreview)) that renders a sandboxed iframe of the rendered React Email — live, against draft content (Sanity `previewDrafts` perspective). name: Pivot email previews to in-component Studio render
description:
Current state: Studio iframe points at worker route /api/email-preview/[type], which fetches Sanity draft via @sanity/preview-url-secret then renders via @react-email/render and returns HTML. Two failure modes hit in v1.2.x: (a) middleware short-circuits all /api/* to under-construction page while apex is parked (smoke + preview broken on prod); (b) STUDIO_ORIGIN_ALLOWLIST CSP frame-ancestors needs hardcoded prod studio URL.

Pivot: render the same React Email components directly in the Studio iframe via @react-email/render in the browser. No worker round-trip, no auth dance, no CSP exception, no middleware exposure.

Scope:
- Audit src/lib/emails/{OrderConfirmation,Day7Delivery,MagicLink,GiftPurchaseConfirmation,GiftClaim,RecipientIntakeReceived,PrivacyExport}.tsx for worker-only imports (env reads, Resend SDK, server-only modules). Remove or factor.
- Expose templates from a shared module (e.g. src/lib/emails/index.ts or lift to a package boundary studio can import without pulling in worker bindings)
- Rewrite studio/views/EmailPreview.tsx to: import the matching template, fetch fixture vars from src/lib/emails/preview-fixtures.ts, render with editorDoc state + PREVIEW_DEFAULTS merge, output via @react-email/render in-browser, set srcdoc on iframe
- Delete src/app/api/email-preview/[type]/route.tsx
- Delete @sanity/preview-url-secret usage (the validatePreviewUrl + createPreviewSecret dance)
- Remove STUDIO_ORIGIN_ALLOWLIST + STUDIO_LOCAL_DEV_ORIGINS env vars from worker config (no longer needed for this path)
- Remove the email-preview CSP frame-ancestors carve-out from middleware
- Pentester re-audit on the new path (preview now renders client-side with Studio-session content; confirm no PII bleed)

Acceptance:
- Becky can preview any of 8 customer emails from production Studio without 404/CSP/auth errors
- Preview refreshes on draft save without round-trip latency
- HTML output identical to current /api/email-preview route output
- Worker bundle size shrinks (worker no longer imports @sanity/preview-url-secret + @react-email/render for the preview path)

Effort: medium-high (~5-8h). Bulk is verifying templates are pure-functional and Studio's bundle config can import them without worker tangle.
result: Shipped via PR #181 (squash 950485f). Studio email preview now renders client-side; worker route + preview-secret + STUDIO_ORIGIN_ALLOWLIST all removed. Pentester clean; one [LOW] alias-narrowing fix folded in.

name: Harden GDPR export per-order throttle against TOCTOU race
description: Security review of P4 (release/v1.16.0, commit 3b86990) found a TOCTOU race in /api/privacy/export: recentExportTimestamp is read before the export_request audit row is written after the work, so concurrent requests with the same valid token can each build a ZIP + R2 object + email (bounded by the CF IP limiter LISTEN_AUTH_SEND_LIMITER). Impact is non-exfiltrating (emails always go to the order owner's registered email) but can redundantly email-bomb the owner. Fix: write the throttle/export_request row before the expensive ZIP/R2/email work, or dedupe via an atomic insert. Also consider a jti replay store if 1-year reusable bearer tokens become a concern. Not a launch blocker.
result: Export throttle row reserved before ZIP/R2/email, shrinking TOCTOU window (55ad9a5). Atomic jti store deferred to follow-up.

name: Listen audio: first-load parallel-request storm trips rate limiter + memory limit
description: Smoke 2026-05-27 (staging, submission 4b3b2bdb): on /listen load the browser opened ~20 parallel GET /api/listen/[id]/audio connections, ALL Canceled at the same instant (19:33:23). Symptoms: (1) 42x 'Error: Worker exceeded memory limit' (4.27MB voice file x ~20 concurrent streaming proxies approaches the 128MB cap), (2) LISTEN_ASSET_LIMITER fired -> user saw 'too many requests' 429, (3) audio recovered and played after the storm; PDF 200. Upstream cdn.sanity.io DOES honor Range (206 + content-range verified), but worker logged 200 on every audio request -> Range likely not forwarded/honored through the proxy, so each connection pulls toward the full file. Investigate client-side cause of the parallel burst (audio element preload + React effect/StrictMode double-mount?) AND why proxy returns 200 not 206. Primary audience is mobile/TikTok 375px where recovery is less certain. Files: src/app/api/listen/[id]/audio/route.ts, proxySanityAsset.ts (gateListenAssetRequest rate limit + forwardRangeHeader), listen page client audio component.
result: Fixed via PR #209 (squash 8357c32). Root cause: <audio preload=metadata> probed media on page load (server component, not React) -> no-Range full-file 200 streams -> ~20 concurrent x 4.27MB hit 128MB workerd cap -> stall/retry cascade -> 60/60s LISTEN_ASSET_LIMITER tripped -> 429. Fix: preload=none (zero load-time requests; play issues sequential Range requests). Proxy/route/rate-limit unchanged. Verified in real Chromium: metadata=1 req on load, none=0 on load, play=1 req Range bytes=0-.

name: Telegram alerting: Worker push + Healthchecks heartbeat
description:
P0. Today's alert path is circular: alerts send FROM hello@withjosephine.com via Resend TO a @withjosephine.com inbox, so an alert about a broken email pipeline dies with the thing it reports. NOTIFICATION_EMAIL is on the same domain.

- OUTSIDE-IN: Healthchecks.io free tier (20 checks) pings the same Telegram channel when a heartbeat goes missing. Covers 'never ran at all' - a dead Worker cannot alert about being dead.

TWO CHANNELS in Max's existing Greatwhale Telegram group: one withjosephine channel with Becky in it (only actionable, plain language), one Max-only (everything, technical). If Becky sees the raw stream she learns to ignore it.

Dedicated bot, NOT the Sage token: separate blast radius, and the sender name reads 'Josephine Alerts' to Becky rather than 'Sage'.

ROUTING - Max immediate: cron dead-man's switch, failed>0, eligible>0 && delivered===0, Stripe not-found, recipientUserId null. Becky immediate: only a failed delivery for her customer, and a hard bounce on a paid order. Nobody: sync-overdue, transient failures that self-heal. Becky queue row unresolved >24h escalates to Max.

Secrets: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN + chat ids as Worker secrets. NOT in URLs.

name: osv-scan is RED on every branch: 28 advisories from 19 days of dependency drift - blocks all staging deploys
description:
BLOCKS DEPLOYMENT, NOT CAUSED BY ANY BRANCH. Found when release/v1.19.5's first CI run failed: lint-and-typecheck, test and storybook all passed; security-audit/osv-scan failed; and because deploy-staging needs [lint-and-typecheck, test, security-audit, storybook], deploy-staging and sanity-validate-staging were SKIPPED. Nothing deployed.

PROOF IT IS DRIFT, NOT CODE: pnpm-lock.yaml and package.json are byte-identical to main (git diff --quiet confirms). main's last CI run was 2026-07-14 and osv-scan passed then; today is 2026-08-02. The advisories were published in the intervening 19 days, so main would fail identically if re-run right now. Any branch pushed today is blocked.

28 advisories. DIRECT deps:
  next    16.2.6  -> 8 advisories, three at CVSS 8.3 (GHSA-6gpp-xcg3-4w24, GHSA-89xv-2m56-2m9x, GHSA-p9j2-gv94-2wf4) plus 8.2 and four 6.x. Fixed in 16.2.11; 16.2.12 is published.
  sharp   0.34.5  -> GHSA-f88m-g3jw-g9cj (7.0). Fixed in 0.35.0 (MINOR bump); 0.35.3 published.
  hono    4.12.26 -> three advisories (6.5 / 6.1 / 4.8). Fixed in 4.12.27; 4.12.33 published.
TRANSITIVE: tar 7.5.16 (GHSA-23hp-3jrh-7fpw at 9.2 - the highest in the set - plus four more), postcss 8.5.12/8.5.15 (7.5), valibot, js-yaml 3.14.2 + 4.2.0, fast-uri (two 7.5s), dompurify, brace-expansion (7.5), linkify-it (7.5).

EVERY ONE HAS A PUBLISHED FIX. That matters because osv-scanner.toml's existing convention is explicit: ignores are only for dev/build-only surfaces with NO upstream fix (elliptic, vite Windows-only, launch-editor, js-yaml 3.x via dead @vercel/frameworks). Adding ignores here would break that convention.

RISK TO FLAG, NOT TO WAVE AWAY: next 16.2.6 -> 16.2.11 is a patch bump inside 16.2.x, but this repo has been burned by exactly this axis. CLAUDE.md records that any non-empty outputFileTracingExcludes on Next 16.2.x + OpenNext 1.19.4 + workerd duplicates AsyncLocalStorage and makes every server render throw. So the bump needs a full cf:build plus mock e2e plus a real-browser hydration check, not just unit tests. sharp is a MINOR bump but build-time only (pnpm optimize-images). hono is a patch and is used by the e2e fixture sidecar.

Also worth noting: deploy-staging hard-depends on security-audit, so a dependency advisory published anywhere in the tree stops all deploys. Whether that coupling is right is a separate question - it is defensible for a site taking payments and holding GDPR data, but it means the deploy path has an external, time-based failure mode nobody controls.
result:
FIXED. osv-scan now reports 'No issues found' with zero unused ignores. Verified locally with the same osv-scanner invocation CI uses.

28 advisories -> 0. Direct bumps: next 16.2.6 -> 16.2.11 (clears 8 advisories incl. three CVSS 8.3), sharp -> 0.35.3, hono -> 4.12.33, @hono/node-server -> 2.0.12. Range-keyed pnpm-workspace overrides for the transitives: tar (the 9.2), postcss, valibot, fast-uri, dompurify, linkify-it, adm-zip, body-parser, js-yaml 3.x.

TWO THINGS THAT NEEDED A SECOND PASS: my first brace-expansion override only covered the 5.x line, but 1.1.14 and 2.1.1 are both still in the tree, so it needed three separate ranges. And bumping hono surfaced @hono/node-server, adm-zip and body-parser advisories that the original scan had not reached.

DROPPED A STALE IGNORE: the js-yaml GHSA-h67p-54hq-rp68 entry claimed 'no 3.x upstream fix exists'. 3.15.0 now exists, so overriding to it made the ignore dead and the scanner started reporting it as unused. Removed rather than left to rot - exactly the drift the file's own convention warns about.

Nothing was ignored to make this pass. Every advisory had a published fix, which is why upgrading was the right call over time-boxed ignores.

VERIFIED, with extra care on the Next bump because CLAUDE.md records that axis (Next 16.2.x + OpenNext + workerd) breaking every server render before: typecheck, lint, 1833 unit tests, 30/30 mock e2e, storybook build, import-graph 34 clean, full cf:build with no AsyncLocalStorage or workStore errors, /book/[readingId] still builds as SSG with 3 slugs, CSP unchanged per route, and a real browser against the production build confirming hydration still works (React attached, Next click fired validation 0 -> 3 aria-invalid, controlled input accepted).

NOT VERIFIED: pnpm optimize-images was not re-run after the sharp 0.34 -> 0.35 minor bump. It is build-time only and regenerating would rewrite committed WebP assets, so it is left for whenever images next change.

STRUCTURAL POINT WORTH A DECISION: deploy-staging hard-depends on security-audit, so any advisory published anywhere in the dependency tree halts all deploys with no code change. Defensible for a site taking payments and holding GDPR data, but it means the deploy path has an external, time-based failure mode. If that is not wanted, the alternative is letting security-audit report without gating deploys.

name: Header name has only 16px of clearance from Back at 375px, and truncation is forbidden
description:
MEASURED at a real 375px viewport, 2026-08-02, all three readings rendered:

  Birth Chart Reading     145.4px wide, clears Back by 32.1px
  Akashic Records Reading 177.1px wide, clears Back by 16.3px  <- worst real case
  'The Akashic Record Reading' (E2E fixture name) 201.2px, clears by 4.2px

PRD D4 predicted the worst case at 171px clearing by 28px. It is actually 177.1px clearing by 16.3px: the live name is plural ('Records'), and the drawn SVG chevron plus its gap makes Back wider than the PRD's model. Absolute centring itself reproduced EXACTLY as specified - 0px horizontal, -0.5px vertical, on every reading at both 375 and 1512.

WHY IT MATTERS: PRD D4 says 'Full names, never truncated'. Becky can rename a reading in Sanity at any time. At 16px of headroom, roughly two extra characters collide the name into the Back control, and there is no truncation, no wrap (whitespace-nowrap) and no min-width guard to absorb it. The fixture name proves the collision point is close, not theoretical.

OPTIONS: cap the block with a max-width plus a smaller phone step; allow a second line for long names; or shrink the phone name below 20px (which worsens the heading inversion in 681ra7bq). Needs a taste call, hence the styling pass.

STATUS 2026-10-01: solved by layout A in c8188a4 (Back is on its own row, so the name cannot meet it). OPEN: measure Back rect vs h1 rect for 'Akashic Records Reading' at a real 375px.

name: Marker-based resend from Studio - remove admin-token paste
description:
P0. MAX'S EXPLICIT CONSTRAINT (2026-08-01): Becky must never set, paste, or fill an admin key in Sanity Studio. Studio is already behind Google-account auth. NOT currently satisfied.

CURRENT STATE: studio/actions/resendCustomerEmail.tsx uses AdminTokenInput (studio/components/AdminTokenInput.tsx, placeholder literally 'Paste the admin token') and sends X-Admin-Token to /api/admin/resend-customer-email, which gates on ADMIN_API_KEY via authorizeAdminToken and returns a bare 404 when unset.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG: setting ADMIN_API_KEY in prod (dex s6139zv4) would unblock the button but leaves Becky pasting a shared static secret into a browser. Rejected per Max.

THE FIX, using this repo's own established precedent: the astro work already solved this exact problem. Sanity v5 Studio cannot authenticate to our app (client.config().token is empty; localStorage fallback failed), so BOTH the admin-token route and the Sanity-session-auth+CORS route were deleted and replaced with a marker pattern - AstroChartInput writes astroChart.regenerateRequestedAt via useClient(), and a cron picks it up. No token, no CORS.

DONE: Becky's resend button writes a marker field on the submission (resend request + email type + requestedAt) via useClient(). A cron performs the send and clears/stamps the marker. Zero secrets in Studio. AdminTokenInput removed from this action. ADMIN_API_KEY remains only for Max's own server-side/CLI seams (delete-user, issue-magic-link, test-mint-token).

Latency cost: up to the cron interval. For a resend that is acceptable; astro-backfill already runs */10.

Est 3h. Supersedes the 0.25h 'just set ADMIN_API_KEY' item.
result: Resend customer email writes emailResendRequest with the Studio session; the */5 cron claims it (ifRevisionId) and sends. Admin resend route and AdminTokenInput deleted.

name: Hero entrance animation blanks below-the-menu content on every reload (perceived load)
description:
SYMPTOM (Max, 2026-07-06, LIVE site): on every full reload — mobile Safari + Chrome AND desktop — everything below the menu is blank for a beat before appearing. Not the old RSC/render-latency issue (that was soft-nav, fixed by Path A).

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed from code, not browser-measured yet): src/components/Hero/Hero.tsx is a 'use client' component using framer-motion (motion/react). Every element below the logo has initial={{opacity:0, y/scale}} + animate with STAGGERED DELAYS up to 1.8s (tagline delay 0.3s, intro 0.75s, CTA 1.0s, scroll-cue 1.8s). framer renders the initial (opacity:0) state during SSR (visible as opacity:0 in the served HTML), so the content — though present in the HTML (Soul Blueprint/Birth Chart/Book a Reading all in the server payload) — stays INVISIBLE until the JS bundle downloads + hydrates, THEN the delayed entrance animation plays. On mobile, hydration latency compounds it. Hero is min-h-svh (full viewport) so it IS the 'below the menu' area on first paint.

NOT part of the problem: ReadingCard.tsx + FaqSection.tsx use AnimatePresence initial={false} — that's the accordion/expand INTERACTION (height animation on click), not an entrance reveal; they don't hide content on load. Scope the fix to Hero.tsx (and check SectionHeading/about+readings sections for any mount-time initial-hidden motion, though those are below fold).

FIX DIRECTIONS (decide aesthetic with Max — it's brand-critical 'quiet archivist' reveal):
(a) BEST perceived-perf: convert the hero entrance from JS/framer (post-hydration) to a pure CSS keyframe animation so the reveal starts at FIRST PAINT with no hydration wait; keep the elegant fade/slide but cap total reveal well under ~600ms.
(b) Or drop the entrance animation on the above-the-fold hero entirely (render visible), keep only interaction animations.
(c) Or minimal: cut the stagger delays (0.3–1.8s -> ~0) + shorten durations so it's a quick subtle fade, not a 2s staggered reveal.
Also: respect prefers-reduced-motion; the logo Image is priority (LCP) — hiding hero text via opacity:0 hurts LCP/CLS perception. Verify the fix with a real-browser (Playwright) timing check on the deployed site (real-browser-smoke), and note this is a UX/brand decision (loop Max / Designer).
result: Fixed via PR #323 (squash 8edc3fa, merged 2026-07-06): hero entrance moved from framer-motion (hydration-gated, SSR opacity:0, stagger to 1.8s) to CSS keyframes starting at first paint, settle <=600ms, prefers-reduced-motion = no animation. Direction (a) chosen by Max. Verified pre-merge: Playwright JS-disabled visible @375px, reduced-motion animationName none, 1821 tests, / static. Deployed-apex re-probe after prod deploy.

name: listen page.test.tsx is a time bomb: fixture deliveredAt aged past the 90-day access TTL
description:
PRE-EXISTING on main, NOT caused by the booking-funnel branch. 6 tests in src/app/(authed)/listen/[id]/page.test.tsx fail with expected 'delivered', received 'expired'.

CAUSE: the OWNED_DELIVERED fixture hardcodes deliveredAt: '2026-04-29T12:00:00Z' (line 37). READING_ACCESS_TTL_MS in src/lib/booking/readingRetention.ts is 90 days from deliveredAt. As of 2026-08-02 that fixture is 94 days old, so isReadingAccessExpired() returns true and every 'delivered' assertion flips to 'expired'. It began failing around 2026-07-28 with no code change.

So main's unit suite is currently RED and will stay red until fixed.

FIX: stop pinning wall-clock. Either use vi.setSystemTime() to freeze now, or derive the fixture date relative to now (e.g. deliveredAt = now - 7 days). Grep the rest of the suite for the same pattern - any other hardcoded date compared against a rolling TTL is the same bug waiting to fire (listen tokens 30d, R2 purge ~120d).
result:
FIXED. Froze Date via vi.useFakeTimers({toFake:['Date'], shouldAdvanceTime:true}) + setSystemTime(INSIDE_ACCESS_WINDOW) in beforeEach, useRealTimers in afterEach. Only Date is faked so async still resolves. Suite is green again: 203/203 files, 1828/1828 tests - first fully green run since ~2026-07-28.

ALSO CLOSED THE COVERAGE GAP THAT HID IT: the expired branch had NO deliberate test, so wall-clock drift was the only thing that ever reached it. Added two boundary tests that set the clock explicitly - 'renders the expired card once the access window has passed' (deliveredAt + TTL + 1ms) and 'still renders delivered on the last day inside the access window' (deliveredAt + TTL - 1ms). 16 tests -> 18.

SWEPT THE REST OF THE SUITE PROPERLY rather than by eyeball. 26 test files carry hardcoded ISO dates. Instead of auditing them by hand I built a temporary Date-shifting harness in vitest.setup.ts (env-gated), VALIDATED that it actually moved the clock (offset 0 -> 2026-08-02, offset 400 -> 2027-09-06 via a deliberate failing probe), then ran the whole suite at +400, +1200 and +4000 days.

RESULT: 203/203 and 1828/1828 at every offset. This file was the ONLY wall-clock time bomb; the other 25 pass an explicit now= or don't compare against a rolling window. Harness and probe fully reverted, vitest.setup.ts restored byte-for-byte.

Worth reusing: the env-gated Date shim in vitest.setup.ts is a cheap CI-able guard against this whole bug class if it's ever wanted as a scheduled job.

name: Needs-You queue in Studio desk
description:
P1. Depends on the bounce webhook and emailConfirmedAt. Hana's spec, and the council agreed it ships BEFORE any badge work: a badge only helps if Becky is already looking at the right document; a queue surfaces the work itself.

DONE: a desk list, one row per reading where emailConfirmedAt is null past the expected send window, or a bounce fired. Oldest order first. One button: Resend delivery email. Zero rows means nothing to do.

Cheap because deskStructure.ts:72-138 already builds three filtered document lists in exactly this shape - a fourth is the same pattern, not new machinery.

HONESTY CONSTRAINT (Rania, overrides Hana's original label): the green state must read 'Sent, accepted by mail server', NEVER 'Delivered'. Resend's email.delivered means the receiving MX accepted the message. Gmail spam-foldering after that is invisible to us and to Resend. Do not overclaim.

Est 4h.

MAX 2026-10-04 (point 8, ships in release/v1.21.0 as Step 1b, after the Step 1 trigger + safe-retry commit): Studio gets a "Failed sends" section: every customer email that did not go out (order confirmation and day-7; Resend errors, unrecorded sends past the ~20h cutoff, bounces and complaints from 0cffo69s), with the data needed to debug it (email type, recipient, attempt and failure times, attempt count, Resend error code and message or bounce type, Resend email id). Becky can correct the customer's email address and resend from there, through the marker pattern (no admin token, tn2c9wys). Assumptions to confirm with Max: covers both customer emails, and a corrected address updates the submission everywhere (D1, Sanity, user record) so later magic-link re-access also uses it.

From the Step 1 safe-retry review (cc7cec6), fold into Step 1b: (a) freeze the email at attempt time: render the reading delivery email once when the attempt is stored and resend exactly that body on retries, so a Sanity copy edit, a name change or a Sanity fetch fallback between retries cannot turn a retry into Resend 409 invalid_idempotent_request; clear the stored body after the send is recorded. (b) A 409 invalid_idempotent_request means Resend already holds a request under this key: show it in Failed sends as "may already have been sent, check Resend" rather than a plain failure. (c) deliver-requested returns 200 even when sends fail, so the Sentry cron monitor never flags them; report failures to Sentry (or a non-200) so Max sees them, alongside the Studio list.
result: Failed sends list in Studio (open failures, oldest payment first), failure details per email, address correction (D1, Sanity, user) and marker-based resend; Step 1 follow-ups (a) frozen body per attempt, (b) 409 invalid_idempotent_request shows as may already have been sent, (c) failures reported to Sentry. Not browser-checked: Studio list and dialog (Max walks it on staging).

name: Speed up sandbox e2e (~14min today, target <8min)
description:

name: Storybook page-level stories — primary UX/UI review surface
description:
WHY (the win Max named, 2026-05-23):
"See the design and tweak it" is currently expensive — every iteration requires pnpm dev, manually navigating to the page, seeding the right state in D1/Sanity, then hot-reloading. For Becky/Max-driven UX review on pages like /listen, /book, /intake, /letter, /thank-you, /my-gifts, /my-readings, that loop is too slow to actually try variations.

Storybook with mocked Sanity data turns this into: open the story, edit the component file, see the change in <1s with deterministic mock data. Becky doesn't have to be in the loop to provide fixtures.

POSITIONING (locked 2026-05-23):
This is a GATE for page-level UX/UI review work, not launch-blocking on its own. Going forward, "review the UX of page X" defaults to "do it in Storybook with the mocked story for page X." If a page doesn't have a story yet, the first task in any UX-review for that page is to add the story.

Exceptions: the U3/U4/U5/U7/U8 launch-blocking UX punch list (Epic wz9t979j) ships through the live dev server because Storybook setup likely won't beat apex unpark.

SCOPE (locked 2026-05-23):
Pages first, with mocked Sanity data. Components that pages compose get stories implicitly as their pages story. A pure-component-library Phase 2 may come later if Becky wants a design-system catalog, but that's not the immediate win.

Target page set (initial):
- /book/[slug] (entry)
- /letter
- /intake
- /thank-you/[readingId]
- /listen/[id] (incl. all 4 states: cold-visit / check-email / rested / DeliveredSurface)
- /my-gifts (incl. send-now armed, cancel-scheduled armed, claimed, scheduled, paid)
- /my-readings
- /my-readings/[id]

OPEN QUESTIONS (research-gated):
- Storybook version + Next.js App Router + RSC support (9.x latest as of 2026)
- Tailwind v4 + @theme directive wiring into preview-head
- Sanity GROQ mocking strategy: MSW handlers in the browser context (works — workerd-isolate gotcha from CLAUDE.md doesn't apply here), OR Sanity-client mock at the module level, OR prop-level injection of fetched data
- Storybook MCP — confirm canonical one (Storybook team announced an MCP server in 2025), what it exposes, whether it's useful for AI-assisted story authoring
- Routing: how to mock useParams / useSearchParams / next/navigation under @storybook/nextjs
- RSC stories: support landed in 8.4; verify it actually works for our App Router patterns
- Hosting: local-only vs static export deployed somewhere (Cloudflare Pages? GH Pages? Chromatic?) vs visual-regression testing in CI
- Workerd dev-bindings: do they need to be stubbed for stories to load, or does Storybook avoid the worker context entirely?
- Build perf: how Storybook builds against this Next.js codebase + how much it slows the local dev loop

RESUME PATH: research subtask first → plan-discussion subtask reads the research + locks decisions → implementation subtasks get filed AFTER the plan-discussion lands. Implementation tasks are deliberately NOT pre-created — let the research decide what the right shape is.
